key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage concentrated near the buried hole-transport-layer interface in p-i-n perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive degradation screening can guide interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification reducing buried-interface damage and improving UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe degradation at different depths.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality-factor measurements.
Compare perovskite films and devices with different ITO modifiers under UV light-soaking.
evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements localize preferential UV degradation at the HTL interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and show improved film and device stability after interface modification.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or validation across broader operational stress conditions.
paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
